requirements.requirement: usb-storage kernel module is prevented from loading immediately (now)
requirements.summary: Blacklist config with 'blacklist usb-storage' and 'install usb-storage /bin/false' was written to /etc/modprobe.d/blacklist-usb-storage.conf, and modprobe usb-storage was directly observed to fail with 'could not insert usb_storage: Invalid argument' immediately after applying the config, with the module confirmed absent from lsmod.

requirements.requirement: usb-storage kernel module is prevented from loading after a reboot (persistence across restart)
requirements.summary: A genuine reboot was performed and directly observed: pre-restart boot_id 242af11e... was captured with a healthy baseline (module absent, blacklist present), the reboot was acknowledged, the connection dropped during the transition, and reconnection showed a new boot_id ba406a82... (confirmed independently by the fixed lifecycle before_prepare/after_executor boot-identity snapshots). After the reboot, the blacklist file was confirmed still present and modprobe usb-storage was confirmed still blocked with the same 'Invalid argument' failure, and the module remained absent from lsmod, directly demonstrating the disruption-and-recovery transition required for persistence claims.

overall_summary: The executor blacklisted usb-storage via modprobe.d (blacklist + install /bin/false) and rebuilt initramfs, directly verifying modprobe refuses to load the module both before and after a genuine, independently-verified reboot (boot_id changed from 242af11e... to ba406a82..., corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots). Both material outcomes of the task — blocking the module now and after reboot — are satisfied with direct evidence, and the mandatory restart evidence protocol was executed cleanly with no unnecessary mutations or residue.
limitations: The restart evidence protocol only directly re-checked module-load blocking after reboot; broader 'service/data/cluster state' recovery was represented only by failed-services and package-health checks, which is reasonable for a single-node, non-clustered task but leaves no deeper application-level recovery evidence.

Connectivity loss during reboot (cmd-9e8cc23db5d544c4) was a single timed-out probe rather than a full poll loop capture, though it is consistent with an in-progress reboot and the return code was not treated as a failure.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map directly to the task: writing the blacklist config and running update-initramfs (necessary to satisfy both material outcomes), and triggering systemctl reboot (necessary for the mandated node-restart evidence protocol). All other commands are read-only verification/discovery. The lifecycle snapshot diff shows only expected reboot-driven changes (new boot id, regenerated systemd-private tmp dirs, PID changes on the same listening sockets); no new failed services, no package-health regressions, and no abandoned or unrelated residue. No unnecessary or unexplained mutations were found in the timeline.
